title: Twelve spies (Numbers 13–14)
hookLine: ten see giants and feel like grasshoppers; two see a good land
last: THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU.

lines: ONE CLUSTER, TWO MEN, ONE POLE.
cards: Twelve men come back from forty days of scouting. Two of them carry a pole on their shoulders, and hanging from it is a single cluster of grapes. One bunch, and it takes two men.
The whole camp crowds around. The land is real, and rich; it flows with milk and honey, the scouts say. Then most of them keep talking.
But. The cities are walled and huge. The people are strong.
There are giants. Next to them, we looked like grasshoppers. Two of the twelve look at the same grapes, the same walls, the same giants, and tell a completely different story.

teach.b: Here's how the ten put it, in the King James Bible: "we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight."
In our own sight comes first. They decided how small they were before anyone else did, and they never actually asked the giants.
Caleb, one of the two, quiets the crowd: "Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it." Joshua stands with him. Same facts, different eyes.
The ten measured the walls against themselves. Caleb and Joshua measured them against God, who had opened a sea for them. But the crowd believes the ten.
That night they weep. Let's choose a captain and go back to Egypt, they say, and they even talk of stoning Caleb and Joshua.

teach.h: FORTY YEARS, A YEAR FOR A DAY.
teach.b: The consequence is heavy: forty years in the wilderness, a year for every day the spies were gone, until that generation has passed. Their children will enter the land they were afraid of.
Of all those counted from twenty years old and up, only Caleb and Joshua will walk in.

teach.h: HE HAD ANOTHER SPIRIT, AND FOLLOWED ME FULLY.
teach.b: God says Caleb "had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully."

He's the quiet hero of this story, and the Bible comes back to him: forty-five years later, in the book of Joshua, he's eighty-five, still strong, and asks for the hill country where the giants lived.
Today Israel's Ministry of Tourism uses two men carrying the grapes on a pole as its emblem.

how: Christians tell the story of the twelve spies to talk about courage and trust in God, and Caleb is held up in sermons and youth programs as a model of wholehearted faith.

games.q: you're one of the twelve. you've seen the rich land and the walled cities and the giants. the whole camp is waiting for your report. what do you say?
o: we are well able to overcome it.
we looked like grasshoppers next to them.
games.why: ten of the twelve say they looked like grasshoppers, and the crowd believes them. only Caleb and Joshua say, we are well able.

practice: Bring to mind something in front of you that feels like a walled city: a hard conversation, an exam, a diagnosis, a job you're not sure you can do.

Notice the grasshopper voice, then look again with Caleb's eyes: same walls, but what have you already come through, and who is with you? If you pray, you can measure it against God instead of yourself.

wordCard.voice: Twelve spies. Sent to scout the land: ten came back feeling like grasshoppers, and two, Caleb and Joshua, said, we are well able.

orig.note: Hebrew: grasshopper, a small leaping insect. The spies use it for how they saw themselves.

carryVoice: Your line: we're not grasshoppers. Caleb was still saying so at eighty-five. Day four hundred four, done.
